title: Characters of central sequences and Jiang–Su stability
author: Claude Opus 5.5 (Anthropic)
description: An exposition of OpenAI's proof (2026) that the central sequence algebra F_omega(A) of a unital separable C*-algebra A has no characters exactly when A absorbs the Jiang-Su algebra tensorially, which answers a question of Kirchberg and Rørdam. The first lesson states the theorems and two named hypotheses from the literature, proves the facts on maximal tensor products, the irreducible representations of I(2,3), the separable reduction and the commuting copies in F_omega(A), and derives the main theorem and a corollary on infinite tensor powers from the finite theorem: every nonzero unital C*-algebra without characters has a finite maximal tensor power that receives a unital homomorphism from I(2,3). The second lesson treats Cuntz comparison, exact cuts, Gram maps with their supporting homomorphisms in the bidual, and commuting Gram maps. The third proves the Rørdam-Winter criterion in an arbitrary unital C*-algebra. The fourth constructs labels: self-adjoint elements of a tensor power whose images stay linearly independent in every irreducible representation of every larger tensor power. The fifth finds a full square-zero element in a tensor power and a unital homomorphism from the matrix cone with full first corner. The sixth identifies tensor powers of the cone with functions on a cube, moves a matrix algebra across tensor factors, and proves the finite theorem.
prerequisites: course Foundations of von Neumann algebras: C*-algebras, the continuous functional calculus, positivity, quotients, automatic contractivity (lesson Order, local units and quotients of C*-algebras); representations, Schur's lemma, the Gelfand-Naimark theorem, norms in irreducible representations (lesson Building representations from positive functionals); the double commutant theorem, polar decompositions, weakly closed one-sided ideals (lesson The double commutant theorem); the universal enveloping von Neumann algebra (lesson The universal enveloping von Neumann algebra of a C*-algebra and W*-algebras)

course Tensor products of operator algebras: algebraic tensor products (Lemma 1.1 of the first lesson), the minimal norm and the theorem of Murray and von Neumann on factors (Theorems 2.2 and 5.1 of the lesson Tensor products of C*-algebras and the minimal norm)
lesson Regular values and degree modulo two (course Borsuk's conjecture in dimension nine): Sard's theorem and regular level sets (Theorem 2.1, Corollary 2.2, Proposition 3.1)
lesson Norm ultrapowers and a group with property (T) (course Kirchberg's embedding problem): the norm of an ultrapower (Lemma 2.2)
the lessons prove every other fact they use, except the named hypotheses (KR) and (DT) of the first lesson

open_obligations: Named hypothesis (KR): for a unital separable C*-algebra A and a free ultrafilter omega, A is Z-stable if and only if F_omega(A) contains, with the same unit, a separable subhomogeneous C*-algebra without characters (Kirchberg-Rørdam, arXiv:1409.1395v2, Theorem 2.5). Not proved in the programme; the main theorem depends on it in both directions.

Named hypothesis (DT): if the infinite minimal tensor power of a unital separable C*-algebra contains, with the same unit, a subhomogeneous C*-algebra without characters, then it is Z-stable (Dadarlat-Toms, in the form stated by Kirchberg-Rørdam, arXiv:1409.1395v2, Theorem 2.4). Not proved in the programme; only Corollary 2.3 of the first lesson depends on it.

Missing foundation: the Jiang-Su algebra and strongly self-absorbing C*-algebras are not in the programme; the course uses Z only through (KR) and (DT). The finite theorem (Theorem 2.2 of the first lesson) is proved in full and does not use Z.

The programme results that are used (foundations of von Neumann algebras, tensor products of operator algebras, Sard's theorem, norm ultrapowers) are cited with their numbers; their proofs were not checked again for this course.
The exponent m of the finite theorem depends on D and is not bounded; the labels come from Sard's theorem and are not explicit.
The lessons were written and checked by one model in one session; they have not been checked by a second reader.
